record.context_brief: whether tr∩H is contained in p-star
record.original_question: Let H be Green’s H-relation on a semigroup, let ∼tr be the epigroup conjugacy relation, and let ∼p∗ be the transitive closure of the relation a ∼p b defined by factorizations a = uv and b = vu. Must every pair of H-related elements that are ∼tr-conjugate also be ∼p∗-conjugate, that is, is ∼tr ∩ H contained in ∼p∗ for all semigroups?

evidence.quote: We leave as an open problem whether or not ∼tr ∩ H ⊆ ∼p∗.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a semigroup. Recall the following equivalence relations on $S$:

1. Green's relation $\mathcal{H}$: for $a,b\in S$, $a\,\mathcal{H}\,b$ iff $a$ and $b$ generate the same principal left ideal and the same principal right ideal in $S^1$.

2. Primary conjugacy: define $a\sim_p b$ iff there exist $u,v\in S^1$ with $a=uv$ and $b=vu$. Let $\sim_{p^*}$ denote the transitive closure of $\sim_p$ (it is already reflexive and symmetric).

3. Epigroup conjugacy $\sim_{\mathrm{tr}}$: an element $a\in S$ is called a group-bound (epigroup) element if some power $a^n$ lies in a subgroup of $S$; in that case the smallest such subgroup contains a unique idempotent $a^\omega$ and one defines $a^{\omega-1}$ to be the inverse of $a\cdot a^\omega$ in that subgroup, and writes $a^{\omega+k}=a^\omega a^k$ for $k\in\mathbb{Z}$ (when defined). For epigroup elements $a,b\in S$, declare $a\sim_{\mathrm{tr}} b$ iff there exist $g,h\in S^1$ such that $b=g\,a\,h$ and $a=h\,b\,g$, with the additional condition $g\,h\,a^\omega = a^\omega$ and $h\,g\,b^\omega=b^\omega$ (the standard "trace" / epigroup conjugacy relation extending Otto's conjugacy from monoids), and extend $\sim_{\mathrm{tr}}$ to all of $S$ in the usual way so that it becomes an equivalence relation.

Problem. Determine whether, for every semigroup $S$, the inclusion
$$\sim_{\mathrm{tr}}\;\cap\;\mathcal{H}\;\subseteq\;\sim_{p^*}$$
holds. Equivalently, must every pair of $\mathcal{H}$-related elements that are $\sim_{\mathrm{tr}}$-conjugate also be related by some finite chain of primary conjugations $a=c_0\sim_p c_1\sim_p\cdots\sim_p c_n=b$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly stated as an open problem in the source. A web search for related work on conjugacy relations in epigroups (including a 2024 paper by Shah on conjugacy in classes of epigroups and the 2019 work on variants of epigroups and primary conjugacy) did not turn up a resolution of the inclusion $\sim_{\mathrm{tr}}\cap\,\mathcal{H}\subseteq\,\sim_{p^*}$ for general semigroups.

status_evidence.title: On a Notion of Conjugacy in Some Classes of Epigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies inclusions among conjugacy relations in epigroups but does not establish ∼tr ∩ H ⊆ ∼p* in general.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on epigroup conjugacy does not resolve the stated inclusion.

status_evidence.title: Variants of epigroups and primary conjugacy
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses primary conjugacy ∼p and its transitive closure in epigroups.
status_evidence.claim: Background on ∼p and ∼p* without settling the inclusion in question.
